Alright, so I've been mulling this over for a couple of days now, and I think it would make discussions better. Issue is, in order to implement it *correctly*, some major things need to be tweaked.

So firstly, what is a Merged Subverse Crosspost? Because a link could be relevant in multiple subverses, people submit the link to those subverses. However, I feel that the fragmentation of these crossposts could be not only keeping small subverses small, but making it easy for larger subverses to be echo chambers. That's where Merged Subverse Crossposts come in.

Let's say two voaters, Alice and Bob, found a cute cat picture on slimg. Alice posts the image on /v/cats, and Bob posts it in /v/aww. This is where the first change comes in.

* Each link will be hashed to have a unique ID (maybe waterfall?) and stored in a database. The first time the link is used, that submissions will become the "master" that all other submissions with the same link will link to.

So, Alice posts the link first by over an hour, and discussion starts in /v/cats. When Bob posts it to /v/aww, the submission will show up on /v/aww, but it will link to the discussion in /v/cats. Some more changes come into effect from here.

* Each post will still count upvoats and downvoats the way they do now, but when viewing the merged crosspost, it'll show the total number of upvoats and downvoats across all the discussions. So, if Alices discussion has 20 upvoats and 1 downvoat, and Bob's has 1 upvoat, the merged crosspost will show 21 upvoats and 1 downvoat.

* Commenting will have to be tweaked a little bit. Because there will be multiple subverses commenting on a single discussion, there will have to be a way to distinguish where a commenter was commenting from. I was thinking having the subverse name next to the posters name, with a link back to that subverse, so if someone didn't know about that subverse and wanted to check it out, they could.

* Moderating a merged discussion will have to drastically change due to possible abuse, but this change will help in the long run. Because multiple subverses will be moderating a single discussion, there will have to be a voting system put into place for the moderators to delete comments and so forth, so X number of moderators from each subverse would have to agree to do mod actions. This has two major advantages:

1. If a subverse is taken over by a powermod and someone makes a new subverse (like the /v/AskVoat and /v/AskGoat shitstorm), the new subverse could crosspost all the links from the old subverse to basically undo the power the powermod had in that subverse. 2. If a moderator is moderating multiple subverses, they only gets one mod vote. However, it is a known issue that powermods put in alts to get around the 10 subverse limit Voat has. There isn't a good way to get around this, and the only way I can think about getting around this would be to hash the IP Address on a mod vote and only count one unique hash as one vote.

The major advantage of this system would be better discussions. With different viewpoints, the likelihood of an echochamber forming would be low, plus smaller subverses will get more chances to grow if more people can find them within a discussion.
